spec.description: Dashboards for obsessive people

spec.title: Deprecated Api Usage Count
spec.description: Shows deprecated APIs currently being requested. Healthy: the panel is empty. Unhealthy: any series identifies a caller that can break when that API is removed.

spec.title: Non List Latency
spec.description: Shows p95 non-LIST, non-WATCH latency by verb and resource. Healthy: lines stay low and stable. Unhealthy: broad growth points toward shared storage pressure, while one PATCH path pulling away suggests admission. The scope-based SLOs are 1 second for single-object reads and 30 seconds for collection reads; this panel drops scope, so interpret those bars with care.

spec.title: Secret Cache Usage
spec.description: Shows how full each API server's envelope-encryption key cache is. Healthy: steady when KMS encryption is enabled, or flat at zero when it is not. Unhealthy: repeated collapse and recovery alongside slower Secret reads.

spec.title: Consistent reads: cache vs fallback-to-etcd
spec.description: Shows consistent reads served by the watch cache versus reads that fell back to etcd. Healthy: fallback remains quiet and stable. Unhealthy: fallback rises, meaning the cache cannot prove freshness.

spec.title: Terminated watchers by resource
spec.description: Shows watchers terminated because they could not keep up. Healthy: empty or flat at zero. Unhealthy: a sustained rise names resources whose watchers are falling behind.

spec.title: Watch cache init events by resource (reconnect replay cost)
spec.description: Shows watch-cache initial events replayed to reconnecting watchers by resource. Healthy: replay follows ordinary reconnect activity. Unhealthy: a burst or sustained climb indicates a reconnect storm and replay cost.

spec.title: Active watches by resource (top 10)
spec.description: Shows the resources with the most active watches. Healthy: counts are stable and match expected controllers. Unhealthy: a sudden jump or one resource pulling away suggests a watch-heavy client.

spec.title: Watch events: received from etcd vs dispatched to watchers
spec.description: Shows events received from etcd beside events dispatched to watchers. Healthy: fan-out is stable for the workload. Unhealthy: dispatch grows away from received events, revealing amplification from many watchers.

spec.title: LIST waste factor (objects walked per object returned)
spec.description: Shows objects fetched by LIST operations relative to objects returned. Healthy: fetched and returned objects track closely. Unhealthy: a widening gap means selectors are forcing large collection walks for small answers.

spec.title: Storage DB size (client-reported)
spec.description: Shows storage database size as reported to the API server. Healthy: slow, explainable growth that reaches plateaus. Unhealthy: persistent acceleration, especially when storage latency rises with it.

spec.title: Stored objects by resource (top 10)
spec.description: Shows the resources with the largest stored object populations. Healthy: the mix is stable and expected. Unhealthy: one resource grows continuously and correlates with memory, LIST, or storage latency.

spec.title: etcd client errors by operation/resource
spec.description: Shows etcd client errors by operation and resource. Healthy: empty or flat at zero. Unhealthy: sustained errors identify storage-layer failures, distinct from fairness rejection.

spec.title: Storage LIST duration p99 by resource
spec.description: Shows p99 storage-side LIST duration by resource. Healthy: low, stable lines. Unhealthy: one resource rises with collection growth, or all resources rise with shared storage trouble.

spec.title: Response sizes p99 (LIST, by resource)
spec.description: Shows p99 LIST response size by resource. Healthy: each resource stays within its usual stable band. Unhealthy: an abrupt or continuing rise identifies payload growth that increases network and decode cost.

spec.title: Authentication attempts by result
spec.description: Shows authentication attempts by result. Healthy: successes track traffic while failure and error stay quiet. Unhealthy: failure or error rises, distinguishing rejected credentials from authenticator trouble.

spec.title: AuthN / AuthZ duration p99
spec.description: Shows p99 authentication and authorization duration. Healthy: both remain low and stable. Unhealthy: authentication alone rising points to the authenticator path; authorization alone rising points to policy evaluation.

spec.title: TLS handshake errors + request aborts
spec.description: Shows TLS handshake errors and API request aborts. Healthy: empty or flat at zero. Unhealthy: any sustained rise means clients are failing before or during request handling.

spec.title: Request filter duration p99 by filter
spec.description: Shows p99 pre-handler duration by request filter, including audit, identity, authorization, and fairness. Healthy: filters remain stable. Unhealthy: one filter separates from the others and explains added request latency.

spec.title: SLI vs total request duration p99 (non-WATCH)
spec.description: Shows total p99 request duration beside the control-plane SLI duration. Healthy: the lines remain close. Unhealthy: a widening gap means fairness queueing or admission webhooks, which total latency includes and the SLI excludes.

spec.title: Etcd Request Latency
spec.description: Shows API-server-to-etcd request latency by operation. Healthy: low, flat lines with writes usually above reads. Unhealthy: a shared step across operations suggests storage trouble; list-only growth suggests expensive collections.

spec.title: Max Go Threads
spec.description: Shows operating-system threads used by each API server process. Healthy: thread counts change slowly and remain aligned. Unhealthy: a count ratchets upward and does not return, corroborating blocked storage or webhook calls.

spec.title: API server outbound client errors (rest_client, non-2xx)
spec.description: Shows non-success responses from the API server's own outbound calls to webhooks and aggregated APIs. Healthy: low and flat. Unhealthy: sustained growth, especially server errors, means a downstream dependency is failing.

spec.title: Priority level utilisation (fraction of limit)
spec.description: Shows mean seat utilisation for each priority level as a fraction of its effective limit. Healthy: levels retain headroom. Unhealthy: a level approaches full utilisation while its queue and wait time rise.

spec.title: Time Request was in queue by flowschema (p90) - Top Instance
spec.description: Shows p90 time spent waiting for a fairness seat by flow schema. Healthy: wait remains near zero and flat. Unhealthy: sustained growth means admission control, not request execution, is causing latency.

spec.title: Unavailable Apiservice
spec.description: Shows aggregated APIs that were unavailable during the selected interval. Healthy: the panel is empty. Unhealthy: any named APIService means discovery and clients of that API are failing.

spec.title: API Server CPU usage in CPU Seconds
spec.description: Shows CPU cores consumed by each API server process. Healthy: instances track one another with visible headroom. Unhealthy: one instance separates or a line flattens at a ceiling, indicating imbalance or throttling.

spec.title: Effective seat limit (post-lending) vs guaranteed floor
spec.description: Shows each priority level's effective seat ceiling beside its guaranteed floor. Healthy: ceilings remain comfortably above floors while queues stay quiet. Unhealthy: an effective ceiling collapses toward its floor as that level queues.

spec.title: Admission Webhook Admission Duration -Top 4
spec.description: Shows the slowest admission-webhook latency by webhook name. Healthy: low, flat lines. Unhealthy: a webhook rises and stays elevated, adding that delay to every affected write.

spec.title: Total inflight request
spec.description: Shows peak in-flight requests for each API server instance. Healthy: a stable band with instances tracking one another. Unhealthy: one instance diverges or all lines flatten against a concurrency ceiling.

spec.title: API Pod Memory
spec.description: Shows resident memory for each API server process, largely driven by cached objects. Healthy: stable plateaus that move together. Unhealthy: memory climbs without flattening or one instance diverges from its peers.

spec.title: Request Terminations
spec.description: Shows the rate of requests the API server abandoned instead of answering. Healthy: empty or flat at zero. Unhealthy: any sustained rise means clients are losing requests inside the control plane.

spec.title: Rejected Requests -2m
spec.description: Shows fairness rejections by flow schema and reason. Healthy: empty or flat at zero. Unhealthy: any sustained rise means clients are receiving fairness-related failures; the reason label explains why.

spec.title: Rate of addition per second
spec.description: Shows how quickly requests enter fairness queues by instance, priority level, and flow. Healthy: near zero when seats are available. Unhealthy: a sustained arrival rate means the level is continuously operating at its limit.

spec.title: Top executing requests by Flow
spec.description: Shows the busiest executing flows by flow schema and priority level. Healthy: work is spread across modest, stable flows. Unhealthy: one flow dominates a level that is also queueing.

spec.title: Flowcontrol request execution time p90 - Top Instance
spec.description: Shows p90 execution time after a fairness seat is granted. Healthy: low, stable lines consistent with each flow's work. Unhealthy: execution rises while queue wait stays flat, directing attention to storage, webhooks, or API-server work.

spec.title: apiserver request total
spec.description: Shows the busiest API request streams by status, verb, and resource. Healthy: traffic has plausible, changing leaders. Unhealthy: one stream dominates persistently; an unexpected blank panel suggests missing data rather than a healthy idle API server.

spec.title: List Latency
spec.description: Shows p95 LIST latency by resource. Healthy: resource lines stay low and stable. Unhealthy: one resource pulls away, or all resources rise together. Collection reads have the defensible 30-second SLO, but this query does not retain scope, so do not treat one bar as universal.

spec.title: Slowest Requests (P90) - 5min
spec.description: Shows the slowest request classes by p90 latency. Healthy: membership changes while values remain low. Unhealthy: one class stays pinned above the rest or all classes rise together.

spec.title: Requests inqueue
spec.description: Shows requests waiting for a seat in each priority level. Healthy: zero or brief spikes that drain. Unhealthy: a persistent queue means fairness is adding client-visible delay.
